payload.blocks: Only the start of orchestration-skeleton; component-authority, 0118 and 1950 keep going.
payload.headline: Run orchestration-skeleton after 0118, 1950 and component-authority land, since its core files overlap all three?

parts.cause: The planner and the plan's footprint show the overlap is in the plan's core files: apps/fgos/src/wiring/supervision.rs, routing, the plan-contract check, the supervisor and lead skills and the supervision spec (shared with 0118), the Questions crate and spec (shared with 1950, ready), and the runner and workflow specs (shared with component-authority). Narrowing the footprint does not clear it. The planner added all three to blockedBy.

options.cost: 0 lines; the plan stays as landed.
options.does: Keep blockedBy as the planner wrote it. Component-authority runs now beside 0118; orchestration-skeleton starts when 0118, 1950 and component-authority are done.
options.gain: No two lanes write the same hot files, so no merge fights.
options.harm: Orchestration starts later: 0118 cannot close before its measures end, around 14:20 to 16:30 on 2026-11-23.
options.label: Run it after the three land

options.cost: About 5 lines of plan edits; a possible 1950 replan.
options.does: Same as the first option, but drop 1950 from its blockedBy and start orchestration-skeleton right after 0118 and component-authority, holding 1950 until it is done.
options.gain: Orchestration starts about one plan sooner.
options.harm: 1950 (owner communication standard, already ready) waits; the questions spec and crate are written by 0056 first, so 1950 may need a replan.
options.label: Put it ahead of 1950

options.cost: One planner session, about 1 to 2 hours; a second plan.
options.does: Ask the planner to split out every phase that touches the shared files so the rest can run now.
options.harm: Most phases touch wiring/supervision.rs, so little is left to run; the split adds a second plan and integration risk.
options.label: Replan to cut the overlap

parts.recommendation: Run it after the three land. The overlap is in the plan's core, so running in parallel would put two lanes on the same files.

scope.allows: The supervisor keeps orchestration-skeleton blocked until 0118, 1950 and component-authority are done, then admits it.
scope.forbids: Changing the order or scope of any other plan.

parts.what: Your 21:45 order asked to run orchestration-skeleton in parallel with 0118 and component-authority. The planner refreshed the plan but could not set it ready: the ready check refuses it for file overlap.

payload.blocks: Phase 12's last done-when (a real soft rotation of a lead) and disk cleanup; phases 8 to 11 keep running.
payload.headline: Who activates the release with commit 8883c2a62 and removes 0118's five finished worktrees, since my sandbox cannot?

parts.cause: The lead's coordination event a397a486e8f5ba3b asks for both. Activation and worktree removal are not in the supervisor's grant (src/session-host/head-grants.mjs), and my confined sandbox has a read-only git floor: even mailbox send fails with git-floor-probe-failed (Read-only file system).

options.cost: About 10 minutes of owner time on the host.
options.does: On the host: build, stage and activate the release from main, then fgos worktree remove for the five worktrees; lead:SUPERVISOR then reruns the rotation.
options.gain: Phase 12 can close done-when 3 tonight, and disk space comes back.
options.harm: Activating swaps the release under live sessions; heads keep running but pick up the new release on restart.
options.label: Owner activates and cleans up

options.does: Leave it all until the 24-hour measures end and do activation, rotation proof and cleanup at plan close.
options.gain: No release swap during the measures.
options.harm: Phase 12 stays open about one more day; worktrees stay on disk.
options.label: Wait for 0118 to close

parts.recommendation: Owner activates and cleans up, so phase 12 closes tonight and nothing waits for it later.

scope.allows: The owner (or the owner's lead:SUPERVISOR session) runs the activation, the five worktree removals and the rotation rerun.
scope.forbids: The supervisor activating a release or deleting any worktree itself.

parts.what: The 0118 lead landed phase 12c (8883c2a62: a lead successor answers mid-turn through the hook door). Proving it needs a release activation, then lead:SUPERVISOR reruns a real rotation. The lead also lists worktrees p02, p02g, p06, p06f and p12c as safe to remove.
